svg.text: rolling meadow; scattered broadleaf trees, boulders, tufts
A. At fight distance, noon: the ground profile, the cover silhouettes, the far land as a value ladder. The two grey figures are 75 units tall (a fighter): scale only, no character art.
Palette at noon (the world-light tint per sky key multiplies it; lit, mid and shade are the three faces of one surface; the far ladder is each ridge hazed toward the horizon)

Readability (docs/art/dynamic-sky.md section 6): worst aura against any tone 23.0 CIEDE2000 (rule: 20 or more), worst Protagonist or rival body against ground, rock or vegetation 23.4 (rule: 15 or more), over every sky key with the world-light tint.
B. What the fight leaves: scorched (a beam along the ground), cratered (an impact), burned (fire on what grows)
a long black band scorched into the grass, the edge ragged and still
smoking in a thin grey thread; the soil under it is dark brown
a round bowl of brown soil with a raised torn rim and grass divots on it
the grass burnt to ash-grey stubble in a wide patch, trees charred to
black trunks with a few bare branches
C. Destruction in plains: the impact at three moments (burst, peak, settle). Dirt and divots: brown clods and green turf chunks in an arc, a low wide dust cloud in the soil's colour.
D. Where it meets its neighbours (hard steps in colour, never a fade; the cover mixes over about a third of the width)
Sand gives way to dune grass tufts, then grass; one low dune ridge between.
Parkland: lone trees, then groves, then closed forest; the grass shortens under
The green dries to gold in steps; acacias appear among the grass; the first red
Grass breaks into tufts on bare sand; scrub, then dunes; the ground steps from
green to gold in five hard bands.
Foothills: the hills rise in steps, rock outcrops through the grass, fir groves
Sparse spruce on cold grass; moss replaces the grass; the first snow patches in
Pools open in the grass, reeds ring them, the grass grows darker and wetter.
Meadow gives way to moor: heather mounds and bracken among the grass, the first
granite boulders, the ground rising in low humps.
